items.claim: this onboarding email lifts week-two retention

cases.text: One: starter signups from Norway via webinar were emailed 4 March; by 29 March week-two retention ran 5 points above the same cohort a month earlier.
Two: starter signups from Norway via webinar were emailed 5 March; by 30 March week-two retention ran 3 points above the same cohort a month earlier.
Three: starter signups from Norway via webinar were emailed 6 March; by 31 March week-two retention ran 6 points above the same cohort a month earlier.
Four: starter signups from Norway via webinar were emailed 7 March; by 28 March week-two retention ran 4 points above the same cohort a month earlier.

items.confound_note: All four cohorts are starter signups in Norway inside the same March window, so one trial policy covers every case at once. The free trial ran thirty days, four times its length in the earlier period, and a thirty-day trial leaves users still inside their trial at week two, which raises week-two retention on its own. That change reaches all four cohorts because every cohort here signed up on that trial. Each cohort is compared against itself a month earlier, when the shorter trial still applied, so nothing in the evidence separates the email from the trial length. The TRUE item in this family carrying closer_variant 'changed_block' (coherent_true in half the families and diverse_true in the other half, see D-022) names the same thirty-day trial but has every cohort sign up on a paid plan, so the trial length cannot reach them and the comparison holds.
items.notes: Cases are byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closing sentence differs. Closer is CHANGED fact + REACH scope. Confirm the trial extension works as a single confound ONLY because the four cohorts share tier, country, month and channel - one policy change reaches all of them, and the earlier baseline predates it. Across the family CHANGED appears once in a TRUE item and once in a FALSE item, and so does REACH, so no single clause is a label marker.

items.passage:
A growth team's log records four signup cohorts that received the same onboarding email.
One: starter signups from Norway via webinar were emailed 24 March; by 9 March week-two retention ran 5 points above the same cohort a month earlier.
Two: premium signups from Chile via marketplace were emailed 3 July; by 27 July week-two retention ran 3 points above the same cohort a month earlier.
Three: enterprise signups from Vietnam via reseller were emailed 25 October; by 10 October week-two retention ran 6 points above the same cohort a month earlier.
Four: basic signups from Ireland via podcast were emailed 2 December; by 26 December week-two retention ran 4 points above the same cohort a month earlier.
The free trial ran seven days, matching its length in the earlier period exactly, and every cohort here signed up on a paid plan; signup volume and in-app prompts held steady, and nothing else changed.
items.confound_note: In cases one and three the retention figure was read before the email was sent: 9 March precedes 24 March, and 10 October precedes 25 October. Half the evidence therefore describes week-two retention that was already recorded when the onboarding email went out, so it cannot be evidence for that email. Cases two and four are correctly ordered but are not enough on their own.
items.notes: Closer is SAME fact + BLOCK scope, so it names no live confound - the flaw lives entirely in the dates of cases one and three. Check that the reversed dates stay inside their own month so the month dimension still holds four distinct values. A shared confound is unavailable here: four tiers, four countries, four channels and four months share no single event.
